subject: AI & Agents
title: Why LLMs Struggle with Math
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Why LLMs Struggle with Math.

hook.text: An LLM that writes perfect poetry can't reliably multiply 47 × 83. Why?

buildup.text: LLMs process text as tokens, not as numerical values with mathematical properties.

discovery.text: For the model, '47 × 83' is a sequence of symbols, not a computation to execute.

twist.text: It can solve common math problems from memory. Novel ones? It guesses based on similar patterns.

climax.text: Tool use — calling a calculator — solves this. The LLM delegates math to the right tool.

quiz.question: Why do LLMs struggle with arithmetic?
options: They process numbers as text tokens, not as mathematical values
They weren't trained on any math data
They can only handle numbers below 100

details.summary: LLMs struggle with math because they process text tokens, not numerical values. They can reproduce memorized calculations and follow patterns but lack the symbolic computation engine needed for reliable arithmetic.
details.whyItMatters: Math failures reveal a fundamental limitation: LLMs process patterns in text, not abstract mathematical relationships. Understanding this prevents over-reliance on AI for calculations.
takeaways: LLMs process math as text patterns, not numerical computation
They memorize common calculations but fail on novel problems
External tools like code interpreters solve this limitation

faq.question: Why can LLMs solve some math but not all?
faq.answer: Common calculations appear frequently in training data, so the model memorizes their patterns. Novel or large-number calculations require actual computation, which text prediction cannot reliably perform.

faq.question: How are math limitations being addressed?
faq.answer: Code interpreter tools let LLMs write and execute calculation code. Reasoning models spend more tokens on step-by-step work. Specialized math training improves performance but does not replace true symbolic computation.
